glosses: Désirer pour soi les avantages d’autrui.

examples.text: Envier le bonheur, le calme, le repos, les succès d’autrui.
Pendant un demi-siècle, les bourgeoises de Pont-l‘Évêque envièrent à Mme Aubain sa servante Félicité.

glosses: Souhaiter pour soi-même un bonheur, un avantage pareil à celui qu'un autre possède, mais sans être fâché qu’il en jouisse.

examples.text: Thorsavn possède un hôpital moderne que lui envieraient bien des arrondissements de Paris et un Sanatorium pour les tuberculeux.

Cet homme n’est pas heureux, et cependant j’envie son bonheur. Dites-moi ce qu’il y a à répondre à cela, sinon que le bonheur est en nous, en chacun de nous, et que c’est le désir de ce qu’on n’a pas !
— […], mais à Mervale les dix maisons, comme dix vieilles filles revêches, continueraient à s’épier, à s’envier, à s’enfoncer de plus en plus secrètes et solitaires, chaque mois davantage, […].

glosses: Refuser à quelqu’un ce qu’il désire ou demande.

examples.text: Ne m’enviez pas l’honneur de mourir avec vous.

glosses: neidisch sein; etwas haben wollen, das ein anderer hat

examples.text: Ich beneide Matze für seinen Optimismus.
„[…] es sind seit 2015 1,4 Millionen Flüchtlinge dazugekommen. Was wir, auch darum beneidet uns der Rest der Welt übrigens, dann doch erstaunlich gut verkraften, wenn man mal ehrlich ist.“

„Dem Nationalteam der Niederlande droht der K.o. in der WM-Qualifikation. Händeringend wird nach der Entlassung von Bondscoach Danny Blind nach einem Nachfolger gesucht. Wer auch immer es wird, er ist nicht zu beneiden.“
„Auch Pullover besassen nur ein paar Söhne gut betuchter Hoteliers, die man darum benied.“
„Um die direkte Demokratie wird die Schweiz benieden. Jeder Einzelne kann mitbestimmen, kann wählen, gar mittels Initiativen Gesetze schaffen.“
Ich neide ihm das neue Auto nicht; er hat es sich verdient.
Meine Schwester neidete mir die Puppe.
„Ich neide anderen Menschen ihren Wohlstand nicht.“

glosses: Resentful desire of something possessed by another or others (but not limited to material possessions).

examples.text: No bliss enjoyed by us excites his envy more.

Envy, to which the ignoble mind's a slave,
 Is emulation in the learned or brave.
distilling therefrom an acid envy that robbed her napoleon of all its savour.
Theodorus assures Socrates that no envy will prevent the Stranger from responding

glosses: An object of envious notice or feeling.

examples.text: This constitution in former days used to be the envy of the world[.]

Blacke Foryst of Despayr, taking photos of the band
 Put 'em up on Myspace you're the envy of the land

Syre said laūcelot vnto Arthur by this crye that ye haue made ye wyll put vs that ben aboute yow in grete Ieopardy
 for there be many Knyghtes that haue grete enuye to vs
 therfore whan we shal mete at the daye of Iustes there wille be hard skyfte amonge vs

But let me tell the World,
 If he out-liue the enuie of this day,
 England did neuer owe so sweet a hope,
 So much misconstrued in his Wantonnesse.

c. 1631-1636, John Ford, The Fancies Chaste and Noble
Such as cleanliness and decency
Prompt to a virtuous envy.
to lay the envy of the war upon Cicero

glosses: A red-skinned variety of eating apple.
To feel displeasure or hatred towards (someone) for their good fortune or possessions.

examples.text:
Moon and Kim took a cable car together to Heaven Lake, a caldera at the top of the mountain, and walked around the area with their wives and officials from both sides.
Pictures showed Moon and Kim smiling and posing with their wives, and Moon filling a bottle with water from the lake.
“The Chinese envy us because they can’t go down to the lake from their side but we can,” Kim said.
“We should write another chapter of history between the North and the South by reflecting our new history on this Heaven Lake.”

glosses: To resentfully or discontentedly desire (something someone else has that one lacks).

examples.text: I do not envy at their wealth, titles, offices;[…]let me live quiet and at ease.
Who envy at the prosperity of the wicked?

glosses: To give (something) to (someone) grudgingly or reluctantly; to begrudge.

examples.text:
But that sweet Cordiall, which can restore
 A loue-sick hart, she did to him enuy[…].

glosses: To show malice or ill will; to rail.

examples.text: He has[…]envied against the people.

glosses: To do harm to; to injure; to disparage.

examples.text:
If I make a lie
 To gain your love and envy my best mistress,
 Put me against a wall.
Both jealous of my love, envied each other

Let later age that noble vse enuie,
Vile rancour to auoid, and cruell surquedrie
